notes: Prospect summary: large fintech with strict residency + audit; wants dedicated capacity so inference costs and tail latency are predictable.
Primary targets: achieve p95 latency <120ms for trader chat (typical payload ~512 tokens), sustain 3K concurrent users during market open spikes.
Throughput requirements: baseline steady-state 6k tokens/sec, burst capacity to 20k tokens/sec for 30-60s windows. Preferred SLOs: p50 <40ms, p95 <120ms, p99 <300ms.

Reserved GPU planning: SE recommends 12xA10G-equivalent for rwx-13b-int8 profile, or 8xA100 (80GB) for base-llama-70b-q4 with persistent KV cache. Customer leans toward fewer large GPUs to simplify memory + context length support.
Model tuning notes: testing two families:
- rwx-13b-int8: good steady throughput, lower mem footprint, needs batching tuned (batch size 8–16) and aggressive KV cache reuse to hit p95 target.

- base-llama-70b-q4: higher single-request latency but better quality on reranking. Requires context length 2048 for some workflows; evaluating q4_0 vs q4_k_mixed quantization for tail latency trade-offs.

Quantization concerns: Auric's ML team asks for Redwood to guarantee behavior for q4 profiles under Dedicated (no silent accuracy regressions). Want recommendations: q4m vs int8, fallback profiles when quantized model fails evals.

KV cache / batching: they require warm-cache persistence across node restarts for sticky trader sessions; prefer pre-warmed cache + continuous batching windows during bursts. SE suggested 'cache pinning' on dedicated nodes and 150ms batching window cap to avoid latency regressions.

SLA negotiation points: customer asks for credit/financial remedies tied to p95 breaches during market hours; Redwood legal proposed tiered credits but customer pushing for higher caps and explicit warm-up behavior in SLA.
Data controls: all chats must be retained 90 days with audit logging and ability to purge by ID. KMS integration required for key rotation.
